base.combos: Combining Inferno Tower with support units like Knight or Valkyrie allows the tankier allies to survive and clean up any fragile support troops left after the primary threat is destroyed. Against large pushes, placing the Inferno Tower on the bridge line forces opponents to commit their main win condition early, making subsequent counter-attacks easier to manage. Use it in conjunction with anti-air Wizard or Musketeer to ensure surrounding swarm units are eliminated.
tips: Be mindful of its vulnerability to high damage spells like Rocket or Lightning; try to predict or draw out opponent spell usage on the tower itself.
When setting up a defense, place your Inferno Tower where it benefits from an initial target that keeps it engaged (e.g., forcing a push towards one lane).
Utilize the lure of the Inferno Tower: if an opponent uses an anti-building troop, send in another unit to distract them or confirm they have committed their full answer.

base.how_it_works: The Knight spawns a single, ground-targeting melee unit that has significantly increased health and reduced speed. This unit remains on the ground and can only target other units, not buildings.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, deploy him to tank large enemy pushes or act as reliable support for building-targeted troops like Hog Rider or Battle Ram. Defensively, he is a primary single-target tank capable of blocking spells that would otherwise hit weaker troops. When facing Goblin Barrel, positioning him near the edge can allow him to target the bottommost Goblin first, distributing damage.
base.counters: Splash units (like Wizard or Bomber) are effective because they attack both the Knight and any supporting unit behind him simultaneously. Kiting units (like Ice Golem) counter his tanking ability by separating him from the main attacking force, allowing defenses to address him separately. High-damage dealers with high single-target focus can kill a distracted Knight quickly.
base.combos: Pairing the Knight with Goblin Barrel is excellent because his high health allows him to tank opposing Crown Tower hits, making the Goblins harder to eliminate with small spells. Using him with building-targeting units helps force opponents to commit defensive spells or troops, allowing for significant damage to the tower while he absorbs attention. He also synergizes with Electro Wizard, as E-Wiz's stun can reset enemies to re-target and attack the Knight.
tips: Positioning him near the edge of the arena allows him to target the Goblin Barrel's bottommost unit first, maximizing damage distribution on defense.
When facing a threat like Goblin Drill, deploying the Knight forces opponents into a difficult decision: counter the single-target tank or let him chip away at their tower.
Due to his inability to hit air units, be mindful of aerial threats when committing him to a defensive push.

evolution.what_changes: The Evolved Knight gains a special shield that reduces incoming damage when he is not attacking. This reduction effect lasts until the Evolved Knight successfully deals damage to an enemy.
evolution.evo_slot_value: Its reduced damage on defense allows it to be strategically positioned away from troops, enabling allied support units and Crown Towers to chip down enemy threats more efficiently. However, dedicating this slot may be less valuable if the deck composition already contains other specialized defensive options that benefit equally from increased resilience.
evolution.how_to_use: On defense, it is preferred to place the Evolved Knight away from allied troops so that he can receive reduced damage until he reaches the attacking enemy troop, allowing allies to chip down enemies without risk of targeting support units or towers.
evolution.counters: The primary difference is its increased resilience; while Minions and Bats still take time to defeat it because they cannot force the shield to deactivate, ground melee troops may deal reduced initial damage, although ranged units can still capitalize on this setup.
tips: Kiting with an Ice Golem is less effective than the regular Knight due to the Evo's shield; instead, position the Ice Golem to keep the Evolved Knight engaged until all available DPS can deplete his health before damage reduction reactivates.
The high HP makes it useful for protecting lower health support troops against spells like Lightning, potentially allowing the remaining hitpoints to be used in a subsequent push.

hero.what_changes: The Hero Knight no longer has the 65% damage reduction when not attacking, making it more vulnerable to ranged troop engagement.
hero.hero_ability: Activating Triumphant Taunt costs 2 Elixir and can be triggered at any time. It grants a shield and taunts all nearby enemies and buildings in a 7.5-tile range for 5 seconds. The ability has a 25-second cooldown after the duration ends.
hero.ability_timing: Optimal timing is to use it when enemy troops or buildings are clustered, forcing them to attack him, allowing allies to focus damage safely. Using it incorrectly can leave him vulnerable if his shield is destroyed before the intended threat window closes.
hero.hero_slot_value: The Hero Knight's high survivability and ability control make it excellent for stabilizing critical engagements or ensuring follow-up pushes succeed across different lanes. However, its reliance on specific placement or timing makes consistently maximizing its value difficult compared to pure damage dealers.
hero.counters: While the base card still faces pressure from spells and high single-target focus, the Hero Knight is especially resilient against multiple-hit spells (like Poison) because his shield can withstand them; however, continuous attack spawning units are slightly more effective.
tips: Using Triumphant Taunt on a push attacking an opponent's tower forces enemy attention onto him, allowing allies to deal significant chip damage without risk of being spammed by spells.
The Hero Knight can be positioned proactively in one lane to draw enemy focus, clearing the path and drawing attention away from your main offensive push in the other lane.

base.how_it_works: The Lava Hound is an air troop that attacks buildings, spawning a slow, single-target unit upon deployment. When this initial unit is defeated, it bursts into six spread-out Lava Pups, which are the primary damage dealers.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, deploy the Lava Hound to serve as a high-HP shield for fragile air troops (like Minion Horde or Mega Minion) so they can reach and hit opponent towers. Defensively, it is best used in combo with other support units, as sending it alone is easily countered. Always be aware that its low sight range means it can bypass some building placements.
base.counters: Inferno Tower excels by dealing high damage to the Lava Hound without taking significant return damage. Zap and Arrows are devastating because they deal high area damage, quickly eliminating all spawned Lava Pups, which deal critical damage if left unchecked. Troops like Executioner or Tornado can group and destroy both the parent Hound and its pups efficiently.
base.combos: Pairing the Lava Hound with Lightning is excellent for removing defensive threats like Inferno Towers and glass cannons that target key support units. Using a combo like Tornado and Executioner effectively groups all surrounding troops, allowing the Executor to simultaneously damage the main Hound and the subsequent batch of spawned Pups. Adding a second tank (like Miner) alongside the Lava Hound maximizes the Lavas Pups' secondary damage potential.
tips: Use Zap precisely on the moment the Lava Hound dies to stun and disrupt the immediate deployment and fighting of the Lava Pups.
If you can predict it, sending Minions to distract or destroy the Inferno Tower/support units first allows the Lava Hound to continue its primary job of damaging the tower.
Be cautious with large pushes; protect your high-value air troops (like Balloon) from swarm damage using support units like Electro Dragon before they engage the main enemy force.

base.how_it_works: Lightning targets up to three enemy troops or buildings with the highest hitpoints within its medium-radius area. When cast, it deals multi-damage and stuns targeted enemies for 0.5 seconds. The spell prioritizes high HP units and can strike multiple separate entities.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, use Lightning to finish off Crown Towers or eliminate support troops like the Wizard or Electro Dragon next to a tower. Defensively, it is highly effective against clustered, fragile supports (such as three Musketeers) for damage or elimination. Always be mindful of your target count; using it on only one or two targets significantly reduces its value.
base.counters: Spells with a large area are sometimes useful for clearing the board, but overall, Lightning is countered by high-HP units like Golem and Mega Knight, as these survive the initial damage. Furthermore, placing an absorbing card like Goblin Cage in the radius can tank multiple strikes, allowing troops to continue attacking while minimizing chip damage.
base.combos: Pairing it with a reliable push (like those involving Lava Hound) allows Lightning to quickly eliminate dangerous, backline threats such as the Wizard or Electro Dragon. For massive defensive bursts, combining it with cheap swarms helps clear fragile units and maintain Elixir advantage by eliminating critical support pieces.
tips: To avoid damaging your own tower when aiming for a Crown Tower late-game, cast Lightning towards the corner of the target area to minimize collateral hits.
When targeting multiple separated units (like Battle Ram and Barbarians), be aware that Lightning will hit each as separate entities due to its multi-target nature.
Due to its high Elixir cost, only deploy Lightning when you can guarantee a beneficial target count of three or more enemies in the desired radius.

base.how_it_works: Little Prince is a ground troop that fires from range using a crossbow, gaining increased firing speed when he remains stationary in place.
base.champion_ability: For an additional 3 Elixir (after playing the Little Prince), he can activate Royal Rescue, which summons Guardienne—a tank with Knight-comparable stats. After a brief delay, Guardienne charges out from behind him, dealing moderate damage and knocking back opposing ground troops by up to two tiles.
base.ability_timing: The ability is best used proactively or defensively against large ground threats that build up damage on the King/Crown Tower (e.g., Golem, Giant). Activating it poorly wastes the knockback potential, allowing high-damage units to hit the towers unimpeded.
base.how_to_use: Deploying him as a standard troop provides steady chip damage and utility for minor threats. Utilizing his Champion ability is primarily defensive/disruptive, creating a strong counterpunch unit with Guardienne that can anchor a defense or secure an elixir advantage.
base.counters: The Bowler is highly effective because it can hit both the Little Prince and Guardienne simultaneously, while its own knockback resets the little prince's firing ramp-up. Strong spells (like Fireball) are also significant counters due to his moderate base health.
base.combos: Pairing him with tanky threats allows them to survive high damage and utilize Guardienne for massive counterattacks. Against large tanks, the combo works by using Royal Rescue to push enemy units out of range and protecting them from direct tower fire.
base.tips:
Do not neglect the initial little prince; without activating the ability, he provides reliable ranged damage that should be utilized in all offensive pushes.
Remember that while Guardienne is a powerful counter-threat, she eventually stays in the arena until removed, making proper placement key.
Use knockback specifically to reset ramp-up attacks or reposition slow ground threats away from your tower.

base.how_it_works: Lumberjack is a ground-targeting melee troop that spawns a fast-moving unit with high hitpoints and damage. Upon its defeat, it deploys a 'Rage' spell effect that increases the attack speed and damage output of other nearby troops without additional Elixir cost.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, deploy Lumberjack at the front of an advancing push so its death triggers Rage onto multiple accompanying troops, amplifying their damage significantly. Defensively, placing him near your Crown Tower ensures that his resulting Rage is focused on speeding up and damaging your own tower's attack rate. Due to his utility, it is best used in conjunction with a win condition or support troop rather than alone.
base.counters: Spells like Rocket are effective for positive Elixir trades by targeting the entire push group. Swarms such as Minion Horde can defeat the initial unit while maintaining high DPS against any remaining units. For maximum safety, combining Tornado with a spell (like Rocket) allows the player to eliminate the threat while controlling the positioning of all involved cards.
base.combos: Pairing Lumberjack with Balloon creates the 'LumberLoon' combo: placing him first forces an early counter-attack that maximizes Rage damage when he dies. Using Minion Horde behind Lumberjack lets the troop act as a tank, drawing attention before the swarms eliminate it and deal massive tower damage. For extreme synergy, using Ice Golem to distract the opponent can set up the attack for Minions or other low-HP troops.
tips: Use Lumberjack early in Double Elixir time (the final 60 seconds) to maximize the potential impact of Rage on critical push cycles.
When defending with a tank, place Lumberjack slightly ahead but not too far, ensuring it remains within range to benefit from its own Rage activation upon death.
Understand that while fast, his high-damage output is mitigated by direct targeting; always be prepared for quick spell removal or swarms.

evolution.what_changes: When destroyed, the evolved Lumberjack spawns an invisible Ghost that has unlimited health and cannot be targeted by troops, buildings, or towers (but can be affected by spells). The Ghost remains within its own Rage spell radius and disappears after a short time.
evolution.evo_slot_value: The unique untargetable Ghost provides significant sustained damage potential against squishy units and mini-tanks. However, the value of this Evolution might be limited in scenarios where quick counter-pushing or consistent magical zoning is required by the deck strategy.
evolution.counters: The general countering methods still apply; players should focus on luring the Ghost out of the Rage radius or slowing it down to waste its duration, which can be done with various spells or slow effects.
tips: Be careful when pulling the evolved Lumberjack toward your King Tower, as the invisible Ghost will deal significant damage if not pulled immediately after the initial Rage Spell is deployed.
When defending with the Evolved Lumberjack, it can be advantageous to deploy it directly onto enemy troops rather than kiting it away.

base.how_it_works: The Magic Archer launches long-ranged arrows that pierce through all enemy units and structures in their path. It is an air-targeting, ground troop with moderate hitpoints and damage, making it highly effective at dealing continuous area damage.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, position the Magic Archer to maximize its range by placing it on the inner side of the bridge or near key structures to strike deep into opponent territory. Defensively, use him to safely snipe high-priority defensive structures (like Mortars) from a distance that keeps him out of immediate counterspell range. A situational tip is positioning him behind your King's Tower; this forces the enemy to commit expensive spells just to neutralize him.
base.counters: High damage/area control spells like Fireball or Poison can completely destroy it, but only use them if they simultaneously hit a higher-value target (like the opponent's tower). The Barbarian Barrel is effective at forcing a favorable trade by hitting the Magic Archer and having the Barbarian pop up to distract him. Void provides reliable damage that forces the opponent to dedicate spells or troops to its removal.
base.combos: Placing Magic Archer with cycle units allows you to maintain continuous pressure and build chip damage over time, keeping the enemy focused on your tower placement. Combining him with tanks (like Golem) ensures he has adequate battlefield range and survivability while providing consistent support fire for the advance. For maximum safety, placing him behind the King's Tower helps protect him from opponent spells until you are ready to strike.
tips: Use his ability to target structures in the other lane when crossing the bridge; this unexpected cross-lane damage is highly valuable for chip damage.
When defending against a large swarm, utilize his multi-target piercing damage by positioning him to attack multiple units simultaneously rather than focusing on one.
Be mindful of its vulnerability to Poison and Fireball during massive pushes, and use defensive structures or other units nearby (like the King's Tower) if you anticipate immediate spell usage.

hero.what_changes: The Hero Magic Archer has the same stats as the base card.
hero.hero_ability: With an activation cost of 2 Elixir, the hero summons a decoy while darting back and fires a triple shot on its next attack. The ability is player-activated.
hero.ability_timing: It can be activated when precise positioning or distraction is needed to deal surprise damage or guarantee high chip damage. Activating it at the wrong time wastes the burst of damage, making the opponent's reaction timing more unpredictable.
hero.hero_slot_value: The enhanced tactical options provided by Hero abilities make placement valuable for highly consistent pressure and flexible threat management. Its value is reduced if the current deck composition already provides superior defensive flexibility or proactive control tools.
hero.counters: No specific changes to counterplay are mentioned for the Hero version.
tips: Use the decoy mechanism during aggressive pushes to draw out opponent spell focus and force an immediate reaction.
The triple shot provides burst damage ideal for finishing off low-HP targets or maximizing structural chip over time.

base.how_it_works: Mega Knight is a high-HP, ground-targeting troop that spawns dealing massive 360° area damage and knockback upon deployment. If positioned strategically between 3.5 and 5 tiles of ground units, it will stop and execute a charged jump attack, dealing double damage and inflicting additional knockback.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, use Mega Knight to initiate powerful pushes or close out buildings by leveraging its high spawn damage against similarly-leveled structures. Defensively, its primary value is using its knockback and area damage to instantly remove critical support units (like glass cannons) from the battlefield, rather than engaging large tanks. Always save it for a moment where you can guarantee maximal impact on enemy synergy or weak points.
base.counters: Against ranged threats like Wizard or Musketeer, deploying them far away allows Mega Knight's spawn damage to focus on clustering ground troops that survive the initial blast but not the jump. Air units such as Minions or Bats are completely safe counters because Mega Knight has zero ability to attack air. Furthermore, highly specialized single-target killers (like Sparky) can overwhelm its immense HP if used effectively.
base.combos: Combining Mega Knight with Inferno Dragon creates powerful synergy by allowing the ground splash damage of MK to take out ranged glass cannons that threaten the otherwise weak ID. Similarly, pairing it with a card like Electro Wizard ensures coverage against air threats and adds necessary magic damage to secure favorable trades or counter-pushes.
base.tips: For maximum impact on enemy support troops (e.g., Elite Barbarians), position Mega Knight so its jump attack can hit both units in the same direction, maximizing knockback utility. Do not waste a jump on tanks; use it specifically against high-value groupings of support or mid-health infantry for the best damage output. Consider keeping an inexpensive spell like Arrows ready to eliminate air swarm counters that bypass the Mega Knight's ground focus.

evolution.what_changes: The Evolved Mega Knight adds an uppercut attack upon every hit that launches the targeted troop back 4 tiles toward the nearest enemy Crown Tower. This pushback and upcutt can be used to reposition bulky win conditions, putting them into range for a follow-up jump.
evolution.evo_slot_value: This Evolution is invaluable defensively because its uppercut can repeatedly disrupt and launch major pushes, often destroying the foundation of an opponent's offense. However, it might not be the best use of the evo slot if the player's primary defensive needs are against dedicated air threats or ground swarms that do not rely on a central tank push.
evolution.how_to_use: Deploying further from the tower when fighting troops like Zappies, Magic Archer, or Mother Witch can maximize the damage dealt by its spawn impact. If using it to counter Royal Recruits, consider using an Ice Golem to gather them together so that the Evolved Mega Knight can launch directly on top of the entire swarm.
evolution.counters: The Evolved Mega Knight remains susceptible to air troops like Minions and Bats; however, its 4-tile pushback consistently interrupts mini tanks like Mini P.E.K.K.A., leaving them vulnerable to a follow-up jump.
tips: If facing heavy ground swarms such as Barbarians or Royal Recruits, be cautious because the uppercut only pushes back one target at a time, requiring careful positioning to prevent repeated jumps.
For highly valuable troops with high health and DPS like Golem, P.E.K.K.A., or Giant Skeleton, use the Evolved Mega Knight to force them off the Crown Tower due to its pushback effect.

base.how_it_works: The Mega Minion spawns a single-target, air-targeting melee troop with moderate hitpoints and high damage. It targets enemy troops or structures, making it a potent aerial threat that can deal significant chip damage to towers.
base.how_to_use: Use the Mega Minion primarily defensively to counter ground pushes and clear out low-to-medium HP units, leveraging its spell resistance. If deployed offensively, use it as support damage, particularly placing it over ranged air troops like Musketeer or Wizard to negate their range advantage. Positioning against enemy defenses or structures is often more valuable than attempting a solo push.
base.counters: Cards with splash damage (e.g., Zap, Giant Snowball) are effective for positive elixir trades by destroying the Mega Minion before it reaches optimal positions. Cheap air-targeting troops like Dart Goblin can counter it if placed far enough away to prevent immediate destruction and ensure continued counterattack viability. Since its high damage is slow, distraction tactics using low-HP troops or friendly buildings also work well.
base.combos: Pairing the Mega Minion with Balloon provides powerful synergistic pressure; the Mega Minion eliminates moderate-health defending units while the Balloon deals massive tower damage. It also works well with Lava Hound, as the Mega Minion cleans up any medium-health defenders trying to interrupt the tank or pups, allowing the pups to focus solely on the tower.
tips: Never deploy the Mega Minion alone if you expect a strong defensive push; it's vulnerable and better used behind initial frontline troops.
When counterattacking after using it defensively, be mindful that the Crown Tower may deal damage when it reaches the structure, requiring follow-up pressure.
Consider placing low-cost distraction units (like Skeletons or Bats) slightly ahead of the Mega Minion to manage enemy attention and ensure a positive Elixir trade.

hero.what_changes: The Hero Mega Minion has the same stats as the base card.
hero.hero_ability: Hero Mega Minion's ability, Wounding Warp, costs 2 Elixir. When activated, it warps to the lowest-Hitpoint enemy and deals damage upon arrival.
hero.ability_timing: Activating this hero ability when an enemy unit is grouping or clumped together maximizes the damage dealt to a single target. If used too early on high-HP units, the damage output may be wasted as subsequent low-hitpoint targets are not available.
hero.hero_slot_value: The Hero Mega Minion is valuable for executing precise removal of priority threats by targeting enemies with minimal health. However, if the immediate battlefield lacks any low-hitpoint enemy troops, placing it in hero slot may waste its ability activation.
hero.counters: No changes are specified regarding how this Hero version is countered; general counterplay remains applicable.
tips: Use the ability to eliminate crucial support units (like low-HP spell fodder) deep within the enemy push.
Be mindful of positioning to ensure the lowest-Hitpoint target remaining on the field is a high-priority threat.

base.how_it_works: Mighty Miner is a 4 Elixir ground troop that naturally increases damage over time when focused on a single target. He can shred heavy tanks with his sustained, high-damage attack.
base.champion_ability: The ability, Explosive Escape (costing an additional 1 Elixir), allows him to instantly dig underground and reappear in the horizontally opposite lane. When he disappears, he drops a bomb where he was originally standing; this bomb deals medium area damage, hits both ground and air units, and knocks them back.
base.ability_timing: The optimal time is to use it to reposition unexpectedly or set up a massive counter-push by placing a major threat in the lane he will resurface on. Using it defensively is risky as predictable movements give opponents enough warning to prepare counters.
base.how_to_use: He should be deployed alone at the bridge (or near the enemy tower) to force the opponent to overcommit Elixir for defense. This setup is highly effective both offensively, by guaranteeing placement synergy, and defensively, by allowing him to split-lane pushes.
base.counters: Highly ranged central units like the Musketeer or Electro Wizard defend well because they can hit him regardless of his movement or ability use. Center-placed defensive structures such as Tombstone and Inferno Tower are excellent because they can pull him away from offensive positions.
base.combos: A strong strategy is to deploy Mighty Miner, then activate Explosive Escape, immediately followed by a threat card like Graveyard in the opposite lane. The opponent's defense against him will be weakened and damaged by the bomb explosion, setting up minimal Elixir-cost counterplay.
base.tips: For maximum advantage, place your secondary threat (like Graveyard) first, then activate the ability; this gives time for the spawned units to engage before the tower targets Mighty Miner. Be wary of opponents who are prepared for his escape, as they may have stacked defensive cards or structures ready.

base.how_it_works: The Miner is a ground-targeting, single-target melee troop that deploys from anywhere on the arena floor. It appears as a man carrying a shovel, which allows it to bypass standard deployment restrictions and enables surprise attacks.
base.how_to_use:
Offensively, deploy the Miner to chip damage the Tower or force opponents into fielding defensive troops. Defensively, use it to tank high-damage opposing troops like Princess or Firecracker, especially by placing it on an inner tile to force enemy ranged units to re-target and protect it.
When initiating a push, send a Mine first on the Tower target; this baits opponent responses and helps even out Elixir trades before your main assault.
base.counters: Powerful spell cards (like Lightning or Rocket) are effective because they can eliminate the threat immediately regardless of its placement. Swarm troops or strong splash damage can counter it effectively if it is supporting a single push, preventing it from dealing continuous damage.
base.combos: Pairing Miner with Electro Wizard allows the E-Wiz's stun to force the Tower to retarget onto the Miner, letting the E-Wiz survive longer and maximize damage. Using it with fast backup troops (like Wall Breakers) by placing the Miner centrally can draw fire from both towers, allowing your support units to attack multiple lanes simultaneously.
tips: For surprise attacks, place the Miner on an inner or center tile when targeting a ranged support troop; this forces the enemy to re-target their unit onto it for protection.
Sending the Miner first with a spell cast on the Tower is great for baiting and forcing out the opponent's intended counter/defense, while simultaneously dealing minor chip damage.
Never send the Miner alone against high-damage troops like Bowler or Sparky; this almost guarantees the Miner will be destroyed in an attempt to defeat them or lose control of its location.

base.how_it_works: The Mini P.E.K.K.A is a ground-targeting, melee troop with high hitpoints and extremely high damage output. It moves quickly but attacks slowly, dealing single-target damage.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, deploy the Mini P.E.K.K.A to quickly eliminate high-health tanks like Giants or Golems before they reach your towers. Defensively, use it against medium-sized threats, focusing on support troops first to save its health for a crucial counterpush. Always be mindful of the opponent's push—targeting support units is generally more efficient than engaging the main tank.
base.counters: Spammy swarms (like Goblin Gang) can efficiently defeat it by keeping the trade positive. Utility spells like Poison can deal damage over time to its moderate health pool, and cards capable of targeted burst or area control will quickly capitalize on its slow attack speed.
base.combos: Pairing Mini P.E.K.K.A with Skeletons allows a tank tower (like the King Tower) to assist in taking down the troop from range. Against support units, deploying the Mini P.E.K.K.A on the support first can clear the distraction and preserve its health to deal with the main armored threat afterward.
base.tips: Prioritize engaging the weakest link: always aim for the supporting troops (like backpack Spear Goblins) over the primary tank unit first. Since it is ineffective against Evolved Royal Giants, save its deployment or accompany it with a slowing/stunning card if facing that specific evolution. Recognize its slow hit speed and utilize it as an anti-support troop tool rather than solely relying on it to eliminate tanks.

hero.what_changes: The Hero Mini P.E.K.K.A has the same stats as the base card.
hero.hero_ability: After a 1-second delay, activating 'Breakfast Boost' allows it to immediately eat all stored pancakes, granting extra Levels and healing itself for 30%. The card constantly gains progress towards this ability, needing 22 seconds to fill one meter, or 10 seconds of progress per attack. The maximum gain is five Levels across three meters.
hero.ability_timing: Optimal timing involves activating the boost after a significant damage exchange, such as following an opponent's P.E.K.K.A strike, ensuring its counterattack capitalizes on the increased health and damage. Activating it when anticipating enemy spells can be strategically countered by forcing the player to waste the healing benefit.
hero.hero_slot_value: The ability creates powerful potential for controlling Elixir trades against high-value targets like anti-tank troops, making Slot 1 or Slot 2 valuable for generating immediate offensive and defensive spikes. However, dedicating the slot might be suboptimal if the current board state requires a different form of support, such as pure damage dealing.
hero.counters: The ability makes it durable against high-damage single targets like P.E.K.K.A and Prince; however, players must prioritize neutralizing the Hero Mini P.E.K.K.A before its boost can be activated, for example using Rocket.
tips: Utilize synergy with low damage troop units, such as Royal Chef, to force the Mini P.E.K.K.A into constant attacks and accelerate ability meter accumulation.
Be aware of potential crowd control or burst spells (like Rocket) that can OHKO it before the Breakfast Boost is activated.

base.how_it_works: The Minion Horde costs 5 Elixir and deploys six Minions in a hexagon formation. This troop type is highly vulnerable to splash damage but presents significant defensive power due to its high unit count.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, deploy the Minion Horde at an elixir advantage or when opponents are unprepared for a push, maximizing its surprise factor. Defensively, use it to support massive tanks (like Golem) or to distract air-targeting charges like Inferno Tower. When deployed alongside Miner, even one surviving minion can force the opponent to address both threats.
base.counters: Area damage spells such as Arrows are the most reliable counter due to their large area and low cost. Wizard and Executioner work well because a single attack's splash damage deals massive casualties. The Cannoneer is highly effective, capable of one-shot killing every Minion with its high damage output.
base.combos: Pairing Minion Horde with Miner creates dual pressure: the minions draw attention while the Miner forces engagement on both the units and towers. When combined with a spell like Freeze, the horde can deal severe burst damage to the Crown Tower, especially if opponents use cheap spells (like Zap) to counter it.
base.tips: Always be mindful that this card is highly vulnerable; do not deploy it alone for an attack unless you expect very minimal anti-air pressure. Utilize support units like Electro Wizard or Tower Princess when deploying offensively, as they help ensure the Minions survive long enough to hit a large tank. Due to its high burst potential, always aim to surprise your opponent rather than relying on predictable follow-up attempts.

evolution.what_changes: When attacked by the first strike, Minion Horde becomes briefly invincible.
evolution.evo_slot_value: The brief invincibility on first hit provides significant survivability during crucial defensive moments. However, dedicating an evo slot might be less optimal if a different card offers unique defensive utility or offensive synergy for your specific deck composition.
evolution.counters: Based on the provided text, the mechanism of countering Minion Horde appears unchanged by its Evolution status.
tips: Utilize the temporary invincibility to survive unexpected initial damage from opponent's spells or troops.
Time deployment so the first enemy attack lands immediately after use for maximum effect.

base.how_it_works: Minions deploys three single-target, air-targeting troops that attack targets in a triangular formation. These units have low hitpoints and are fast-moving aerial attackers.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, Minions excel at damaging buildings or distracting high-hitpoint troop counters (like Inferno Towers) due to their ability to bypass terrain. Defensively, they function as excellent utility troops that can quickly eliminate support units, such as Cannons or Mortars, especially when the opponent lacks dedicated splash anti-air. Avoid building major counterpushes with them unless you are certain the opponent has insufficient Area of Effect (AoE) anti-air spells.
base.counters:
Spells like Arrows and Royal Delivery are highly effective because Minions' low hitpoints make them vulnerable to damage that destroys multiple units for a neutral Elixir trade. Vines can also handle them, though their effectiveness is reduced if the opponent places higher health troops on the area due to targeting priority mechanics.
Zap or Giant Snowball can weaken Minions enough, allowing friendly single-target units like Tower Princess to execute an instant kill.
base.combos: Pairing Minions with a tank, such as Miner, creates immediate threat pressure by forcing the opponent to address both the direct tower damage and the fragile air units. Using Freeze or similar spells is useful when attacking with Minions, as it disables the opponent's Crown Tower and any nearby support for critical seconds, making follow-up attempts more punishing.
tips: Consider positioning buildings that act as counters (e.g., Tesla, Cannon) near river edges to maximize Minion damage potential on short ranges.
Utilize Minions not just for DPS, but specifically to draw attention and delay key anti-tank support structures like Inferno Towers or Mortars.
Because they bypass the river, understanding map placement is critical; use them to hit buildings positioned in 'dead' spots that otherwise wouldn't be covered.

base.how_it_works: The Mirror is a spell that replicates the last card played by the player, costing an additional Elixir. It maintains the replicated card's base function and abilities while boosting its level one higher than the original.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, use it on cards like Goblin Barrel or Graveyard when you suspect your opponent has limited counter options; this forces them to either waste a high-level single counter or risk multiple failed trades. Defensively, mirroring strong spells (e.g., Earthquake) can negate their intended effect by boosting the replicated spell's power or survivability. It is especially useful when repeating basic units like Fire Spirits, as the level boost dramatically improves their ability to withstand common area damage.
base.counters: Area damage troops such as Wizard and Executioner are excellent counters because they often counter multiple cards simultaneously, bypassing the advantage of leveling up a single unit type. Highly efficient spells (like Zap) can counter the spell's strategic purpose by removing low-level units instantly without needing to assess the card's base effectiveness. Simply having an Elixir advantage allows the opponent to deploy multiple counters before the level boost takes effect.
base.combos: Combining Mirror with high-damage, low-elixir win conditions like Goblin Barrel maximizes the threat because repeating a cheap spell/troop forces your opponent to react with limited resources. Spreading damage using spells such as Earthquake or Fireball works well in conjunction with Mirror by allowing you to dictate which specific units are boosted for maximum immediate impact.
tips: Use it specifically on cards that benefit from extra damage, like Goblin Barrel, since the level boost can turn a moderate threat into an overwhelming force.
When mirroring spells, prioritize repeating control spells (like Zap or Earthquake) to instantly remove key opponent threats rather than simply escalating raw damage.
The ability to use Mirror multiple times in succession allows for unparalleled tempo swing and resource manipulation, demanding precise timing throughout the match.

base.how_it_works: The Monk is a high-HP, melee ground troop that uses a unique 3-hit combo: the first two attacks deal normal damage, while the third strike deals extra damage and knockback. He requires 5 Elixir to deploy.
base.champion_ability: To activate Pensive Protection, the player must spend an additional 1 Elixir after deploying him. This ability grants a significant damage reduction (65%) for a short time and reflects incoming projectile-based ranged attacks back at their source; reflected spells are aimed specifically at the opponent's closest Crown Tower. The ability has a long cooldown of 17 seconds.
base.ability_timing: The optimal timing is proactively, using him as a 'shield' for vulnerable ranged units that usually get weakened by spells. Activating late or reactively can be high-risk, requiring pinpoint timing against powerful spells like Rockets.
base.how_to_use: Deploy the Monk first to establish his presence and start building chip damage with his combo attacks; then activate Pensive Protection when facing expected heavy spell pressure. He excels in both offensive pushes (through combo backfall) and defensive shield roles.
base.counters: Heavy spell damage that does not involve projectiles, such as Poison or certain area-of-effect ground attacks, are the best counters because they bypass his reflection ability. Alternatively, fast cycling troops like Skeleton Army can overwhelm him before he gets time to set up Pensive Protection.
base.combos: Pairing him with cheap ranged units (e.g., Firecracker) maximizes value by allowing the unit to survive spells that would otherwise hit it. Furthermore, placing him near an Elixir Collector or Sparky allows his ability to turn enemy projectiles (like Rockets) back into significant damage against the opponent's towers.
base.tips: Recognize that while he reflects many projectiles, any card placed directly in front of him during Pensive Protection will still be exposed to incoming attack. Use the ability not just for defense, but as a setup tool to facilitate high-damage third hits from his own combo cycle.

base.how_it_works: The Mortar is a long-ranged ground building that deals area damage by launching large boulders. It has high hitpoints and possesses a significant 'blind spot,' meaning it cannot attack any targets positioned very close to itself.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, deploy the Mortar centrally or in an exposed lane to capitalize on its ability to deal splash damage near enemy towers. Defensively, placing it closer to your King's Tower allows it to engage incoming swarms and eliminate structures like Elixir Collectors. Be cautious when using it defensively, as slow attack speed means you must ensure strong distractions are ready.
base.counters: Slow, high-HP building-targeting troops, such as the Ice Golem, can distract the Mortar completely due to its low Damage Per Second (DPS) and the defender's ability to place a unit in front of it. Similarly, fast units like Hog Rider or Ram Rider are difficult for the Mortar to target because they operate within the card's close-range blind spot. Using Lightning or spells that remove buildings can instantly neutralize its threat.
base.combos: Pairing the Mortar with spell cards (like Zap) helps interrupt enemy pushes and deal extra damage, while pulling units into the area maximizes splash potential. Furthermore, using Tornado to draw enemy troops closer to your tower forces them into the Mortar's effective splash range, maximizing damage output in a single push.
tips: Due to its 3.5 second deployment time, play a distraction unit at the absolute last moment to catch the opponent off guard and prevent it from locking onto critical structures.
If you predict an aggressive defense, place the Mortar in the center of your territory (rather than one side) to limit the areas where opposing troops can operate directly on top of it.
When initiating a push with the Royal Giant against the Mortar, attacking in the same lane as the unit is recommended to maintain pressure and prevent flanking.

evolution.what_changes: The Evolved Mortar gains an increased hit speed and, critically, spawns a Goblin with every attack.
evolution.evo_slot_value: The Evo significantly boosts the damage potential, capable of taking down a Crown Tower on its own if left unchecked. However, dedicating this slot might be suboptimal if your deck lacks synergistic tools that can reliably leverage the massive area splash and secondary Goblin damage.
evolution.counters: It remains vulnerable to high-damage buildings like Earthquake, but now also gains synergy with defensive cards such as the Goblin Drill, which can provide an equal Elixir trade while heavily reducing damage dealt to your own towers.
tips: When targeting a Tower Princess, be aware that the spawned Goblins will receive double hits, significantly amplifying the total damage output.
Due to the vulnerability of the spawned Goblins to the King Tower's splash, prioritizing activations that activate your King Tower can reduce future incoming damage.

base.how_it_works: The Mother Witch deploys a single-target, air-targeting troop that curses enemies upon attack. When a cursed enemy unit dies to her, it transforms into a Cursed Hog—a functional mini-tank that fights alongside the Witch.
base.how_to_use: Use her defensively early game on high-value swarm units like Skeletons or Bats; this quickly generates initial pressure while protecting your lanes. Offensively, deploy her behind a main tank (like a Giant) to ensure any remaining swarm troops are forced into combat and convert into secondary attackers. Timing is key: keep her away from the opponent's isolated tower at all costs, as she can be locked onto by ranged units.
base.counters: Mini-tanks like Knight or Mini P.E.K.K.A are effective because they hit hard enough that the Mother Witch cannot damage them quickly enough to trigger multiple curses and subsequent Hog spawns. Similarly, high burst damage troops (like Prince) can overwhelm her before she completes a full cycle of attacks.
base.combos: Support with electric damage, such as Electro Giant, to help apply initial chip damage, making it easier for the Mother Witch to curse targets rapidly. Partnering her with a traditional tank creates a devastating layer of persistent threat: the tank pushes, and the Hogs are spawned in from behind to assist.
tips: Against buildings or stationary threats like Inferno Tower, realize she is only effective if she can target nearby troops that will then trigger the cycle on death.
Remember that sub-troops (like those spawning from an egg) must be directly targeted by her post-spawn to initiate the Cursed Hog conversion.
The secondary Hogs spawned are useful support units but cannot be inflicted with a curse themselves, meaning they lack the proactive utility of the original spell.

base.how_it_works: The Musketeer is a single-target, air and ground troop that attacks from long range with moderate hitpoints and damage. Its high hit speed allows it to deal swift damage against swarms or small units.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, utilize its substantial 6-tile range by positioning slightly off the main lane to snipe opponent towers and eliminate support troops before they reach your core forces. Defensively, leverage its range to attack high-priority threats (like other ranged troops) or clear swarms of low hitpoints units without committing too many resources.
base.counters: Against squishy air/ground damage dealers like Mega Minion or Miniuns, keep Musketeer at a distance to prevent immediate elimination. For multi-target pressure tools such as the Bomber's death damage or Goblin Demolisher, place Musketeer strategically far from their path to avoid residual damage.
base.combos: Pairing Musketeer with mini-tanks (like Knight) ensures that even if she is heavily targeted, she retains adequate life and persistent firepower. Supporting her with high-damage AoE spells or buildings allows the combo to sustain pressure while her range shreds enemy defenses from a safe distance.
tips: Use her long range advantageously by positioning her in the 'pocket'—the area between both players' Princess Towers—to safely harass opponent towers without being targeted by King Tower shots.
Against predictable single-lane pushes, use her to aggressively attack secondary structures or support units on the opposite side of the map to force a defensive pivot from your opponent.
Recognize that while she is excellent against swarms, she may struggle against unit hordes like Minion Horde and need additional clearing spells (like Zap) to maximize efficiency.

evolution.what_changes: The Evolved Musketeer spawns a unit with identical base stats but gains 3 infinite-range attacks that target the closest troop or building in front of her, dealing 1.8 times the damage of her normal attacks.
evolution.evo_slot_value: This Evolution grants powerful sniping abilities that allow it to bypass Crown Towers and attack targets (like Elixir Collectors) behind them, offering unique map control potential. However, dedicating this slot might be less valuable if your current deck composition lacks strong ranged support or requires immediate defensive synergy.
evolution.how_to_use: To maximize the sniper shots, place the Evolved Musketeer at a distance from her intended target to ensure she expends all three charges in a controlled manner. Due to its long range, placing it slightly further than targeted buildings' maximum ranges can help ensure rapid elimination of structures.
evolution.counters: The general application of counters remains true, but specific high-HP units or swarms (like Miniion Horde or Mega Minion) can still eliminate the Evolved Musketeer quickly if positioned directly on top of her.
tips: Its long range allows it to attack structures like Inferno Tower and Mortar using its sniper shots, bypassing placement limitations that restrict normal attacks.
When attacking a Balloon, expend the sniper shots first to negate any Crown Tower damage and potentially leave the unit safe from follow-up support.

hero.what_changes: The Hero Musketeer has the same stats as the base card.
hero.hero_ability: The Hero Musketeer can activate 'Trusty Turret' by spending an additional 3 Elixir. This ability spawns a short-range auto-turret in front of the Musketeer, which lasts for 10 seconds and can be used as both a distraction and a building to attract win conditions. The ability has a cooldown of 22 seconds after its duration ends.
hero.ability_timing: It is advised not to use this ability against an enemy Electro Giant, as this combination worsens the Elixir cost and risks causing the Musketeer damage through abilities like Zap Pack. Optimal usage involves maintaining range, either by defeating opponents without taking damage or forcing them to close the distance using cards like Tornado or Fisherman.
hero.hero_slot_value: The Heroic Musketeer is valuable for establishing tactical map control when placing it in Slot 1 or Slot 2. Conversely, if the immediate battlefield situation does not require attracting win conditions, its specialized ability may make another card a better choice for this high-impact slot.
hero.counters: The Hero Musketeer retains general counters; however, players must be wary of enemies using abilities like Zap Pack or electro-damage sources when the turret is deployed, as these can lure it into danger and increase its effective Elixir cost.
tips: Be aware that deploying this ability against specific electric troop types significantly increases risk to the Musketeer.
Use the spawned turret proactively not just as a distraction, but specifically to draw targetable win conditions away from your primary forces.

base.how_it_works: The Night Witch is a ground-targeting, melee troop that constantly summons Bats (initially 1 second after deployment). These Bats surround her and provide continuous swarm damage. Furthermore, when defeated, she will also spawn an additional Bat.
base.how_to_use: Use the Night Witch defensively to anchor high-HP single troops like Prince or Mega Knight, letting her survive long enough for her high damage to chip away at their health. Offensively, pair her with large tanks (like Giant or Golem) so that she distracts enemy units while the tank pushes toward the tower. Situational timing: Deploy her near the King's Tower to send a single Bat into the opposite lane for light zone protection.
base.counters: Air troops like Minions or Electro Dragon are highly effective counters because they can easily eliminate both the Witch and her summoned Bats, bypassing her ground-only focus. High burst damage spells (like Lightning) work well since she lacks self-sustaining defensive mechanics compared to cards that spawn skeletons. Cards with area denial, such as those that target clusters of units, will help prevent the overwhelming swarm effect.
base.combos: Pairing Night Witch with large tanks like Golem or Giant allows the tank to absorb damage while the Bats distract and chip away at enemy threats to the tank. She also synergizes well with air support like Lava Hound; the bats act as effective distractors against counter-spells aimed at the aerial unit, letting the main threat press forward.
tips: Keep the Night Witch at range from opposing troops' spell damage (like Wizard or Musketeer) to avoid her being instantly removed before she can build up a meaningful swarm.

When making a slow push with a tank, position the Night Witch slightly ahead of the main body and use her focused attention on utility units like Inferno Tower rather than letting them focus on your primary threat.
If using her in an aggressive double-lane setting, understand that while she can spawn a Bat into the opposing lane, this single bat is generally insufficient for sustained harassment.

base.how_it_works: P.E.K.K.A is a single-target, ground-targeting melee unit that features extremely high hitpoints and immense damage. It operates as a slow but incredibly durable heavy tank, capable of dealing massive amounts of damage in one hit.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, deploy P.E.K.K.A behind substantial support troops (like area damage or splash units) to break through enemy defenses and apply overwhelming pressure. Defensively, use her as a hard counter against major ground threats like Golem or Elite Barbarians; she can absorb massive hits while removing durable opponent tanks piece by piece. When cross-river pushing, always include spell bait support cards to distract counters that might ignore the main threat.
base.counters: The Hunter is effective if P.E.K.K.A is protected by a high-HP tank or swarms, allowing it to safely engage from range. Royal Recruits are strong against lone P.E.K.K.A due to their shield mechanics and ability to take hits on both towers simultaneously. Area damage spells like Poison can prevent large enemy swarms from attacking, keeping the pressure consistent.
base.combos: Pairing P.E.K.K.A with support troops such as Executioner or Electro Dragon is powerful because the area damage handles swarms and utility units, allowing P.E.K.K.A to focus on heavy armored targets. Tornado pulls key ranged threats into range of P.E.K.K.A's melee attacks, enabling it to finish off crucial back-line supports that would otherwise survive. Combining the initial tanking power with spells like Poison or Zap ensures continuous chip damage even if the main push is disrupted.
tips: Since she cannot attack air units, always cycle support cards or defensive troops into her deployment plan to protect against Minion Horde or Inferno Dragon setup attempts.
Do not commit P.E.K.K.A alone across the bridge; anticipate and account for grounded swarm bait (like Skeleton Army) which is often used to force an Elixir trade with a spell.
Understand that while she can tank against many shots, her single-target nature makes advanced air units like Electro Dragon or Inferno Dragon extremely dangerous as they ignore her high HP.

evolution.what_changes: The Evolved P.E.K.K.A possesses a unique healing mechanism: after defeating an enemy troop or building, it spawns a butterfly around its sword, healing 3.5%-15% of its original hitpoints. This healing can potentially overheal, allowing the card to achieve up to 50% more hitpoints at its maximum capacity.
evolution.evo_slot_value: The Evolution's combined massive damage and sustained self-healing make it an incredibly powerful wall for both offense and defense, enabling positive Elixir trades by counterattacking. However, dedicating an evo slot might be less optimal if the current meta already has another card that needs an evolution to achieve a much greater tactical impact.
evolution.counters: It remains a hard counter to the Evolved Mega Knight and is particularly effective against the Evolved Goblin Giant, but small to medium ground swarms (like Goblin Gang) can still force it to heal, keeping it healthier for sustained attacks.
tips: Since healing only triggers when an opponent's unit or building is defeated, high DPS troops that prevent the final blow can effectively stall and diminish its ability to recover HP.

While its slow attack rate allows certain grounded troops (like Guards) to survive hits, being able to use it as a distraction against air units helps mitigate risks from multi-hit threats like Inferno Dragon.

base.how_it_works: The Phoenix is an air troop that deploys a single, melee, air-targeting unit. When defeated, it explodes, dealing damage and knockback while spawning a low-health Egg. If the Egg remains undestroyed for 3.8 seconds, it hatches into a new, full-strength Phoenix.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, use the Phoenix in conjunction with other high-damage troops to maximize its initial burst damage and the subsequent explosion/hatch combo. Defensively, deploy it directly over high-priority enemy ranged units (like Witch or Wizard) to bypass continuous spawning or chip down targets quickly. Always be mindful of timing and follow up any successful spawn with immediate support damage to ensure the Egg hatches successfully.
base.counters: Ground targeting troops can kite the Phoenix by engaging its initial form, allowing Crown Towers to deplete its HP before it spawns an Egg. Air swarms (like Minion Horde) or anti-air cards like Wizard/Executioner are highly effective as they overwhelm the unit and destroy the low-health Egg immediately. Any spell with damage equal to or higher than Arrows can reliably counter the Phoenix by destroying the spawned Egg in one shot.
base.combos: The combination of Phoenix and Clone is powerful, allowing a second death explosion that provides extra offensive and defensive utility. Pairing it with Mirror creates an unexpected, often higher-leveled second unit, which increases survivability and makes the original's revival much more likely. Using Tornado to pull targets into the attack radius for both the Witch or Wizard can help quickly neutralize ranged support units.
tips: Always use minimal damage troops (like Skeletons) or simple buildings to protect the Egg from enemy spells, as failure means a significant Elixir loss.
When facing multiple unsupported range cards, position the Phoenix directly over them when deploying to maximize damage and minimize unnecessary tower damage.
Keep in mind that even if it dies to a Crown Tower, defensive spells like Zap or Giant Snowball can provide crucial delays, giving the Egg enough time to revive.

base.how_it_works: Poison is an area-damage spell that deals low damage every second for 8 seconds across a medium radius, affecting both troops and buildings. It also applies a 15% movement speed slow to all enemy units within its area.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, Poison excels at mitigating threats like swarms or utility buildings (e.g., Goblin Hut, Furnace) by damaging them over time and controlling their spawn cycle. While the slow effect is useful defensively, it's generally recommended to save it for predictable defensive pushes in a pinch. Consider placing it ahead of high-speed troops—such as Hog Rider or Lumberjack—to maximize the slowdown and maintain pressure.
base.counters: The Clone is a hard counter because Poison's 8-second duration allows it to take out cloned units and prevent their deployment for the entire spell duration, allowing you to counter the original troop. For high-health tanks like Barbarians or Royal Recruits, Poison can be used defensively as a positive Elixir trade by dealing consistent damage that forces them into unfavorable positions for your Crown Towers.
base.combos: It works well with Graveyard because it shares a similar long duration and covers much of the radius needed to deal continuous chip damage to enemy defenses. Pairing it with Miner allows you to place Poison on different tiles from the Miner's placement, forcing the opponent into indecision about where your real threat is.
base.tips:
Do not use Poison assuming high raw damage; its true value comes from slowing movement and suppressing spawner buildings like Goblin Hut or Furnace.
If attempting a bait, try using it specifically on utility placements (like an Elixir Collector) to limit the opponent's resources and tempo instead of just hitting troops.
Always deploy fast-attacking troops immediately after Poison expires to capitalize on their momentum while the opponent recovers from the slow effect.

base.how_it_works: The Prince is a ground troop that spawns and attacks its target with high damage. After traveling two tiles, it begins charging towards the target, dealing double damage upon impact. It is notable for being able to jump over rivers.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, use the Prince as a counter-attack threat to quickly capitalize on an opponent's empty Elixir or when their defenses are out of rotation. Defensively, deploy him closer to your tower if facing a slow troop; his charging damage will maximize against slower units in this position. Consider dropping the Prince in one lane while applying pressure or forcing defense in an opposite, uncontested lane.
base.counters: Strong and durable troops such as P.E.K.K.A., Mega Knight, Boss Bandit, Giant Skeleton, or Mighty Miner are effective counters due to their high durability and consistency of damage output. Utilizing a stun effect or distraction tank is recommended when facing him in battle, as they can save fragile units from the charge attack. Similarly, while powerful, he is quickly overwhelmed by numerous spawned Goblins after dealing with an Evolved Goblin Giant.
base.combos: Pairing him with high hitpoint tanks like the Giant or Golem allows them to soak up initial hits while the Prince deals damage. A particularly effective combination involves Mega Knight for its splash damage and tanking support, allowing it to clear swarms that otherwise threaten both units. These combos work synergistically because the Mini Knight's jump and charge allow them to easily maintain proximity and pressure.
base.tips: Using lighter spells like Zap or Minion Searchball is highly recommended as a prediction tool to remove swarm cards (e.g., Skeleton Army) before they can overwhelm him. When anticipating an opponent's defensive counter, use the Miner preemptively to distract support troops near their tower, allowing the Prince’s charge path clear to the enemy King Tower. If you expect an opposing push, using a freeze spell on his charging attack is beneficial, as it disables his damage and allows your team to safely eliminate him without worrying about backup units.

base.how_it_works: Princess spawns an air-targeting, very long-ranged ground troop that deals area damage in bursts of three volleys. She has low hitpoints and moderate damage output.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, use her support or siege nature by deploying her at the bridge for early chip damage; this timing is exceptionally difficult for opponents to react to. Defensively, place her on the opposite side of your opponent's push to force them into an immediate and potentially over-committing response. She should be protected with cheap troops like Skeletons or Bats while they absorb initial aggression.
base.counters: Area damage spells (such as The Log, Arrows, Fireball, and Poison) are the most reliable counters because she cannot defend against their blanket effects. Mini P.E.K.K.A is effective for a massive negative Elixir trade; waiting until she reaches the bridge allows him to one-shot her while surviving his first attack. Magic Archer forces trades by dealing damage to her and then counterattacking, forcing the opponent to spend additional Elixir.
base.combos: Zap combined with Princess synergy instantly removes swarms of low HP units, ensuring continuous chip damage or support application. Skeletons provide valuable distraction at the bridge, creating a negative Elixir trade that forces opponents to commit spells or troops unnecessarily. Using her at the opposite side of a push can maximize pressure and force split attention across multiple threats.
tips: When deploying at the bridge for chip damage, note the timing: her first attack is faster than subsequent ones, giving you a critical early edge.
Although she deals moderate damage, remember that allowing her to stay alive on the map for too long results in enormous, cumulative chip damage.
Consider utilizing The Log over Arrows when defending because its area denial effect allows you to hit surrounding supporting units near the bridge.

evolution.what_changes: The Evolution spawns two Archers and an area-damage, air-targeting, very long-ranged ground troop with low hitpoints and moderate damage.
evolution.evo_slot_value: This Evolution provides immediate added pressure by spawning multiple archers and increasing the range of the resulting area-damage unit. It might not be the best use of the Evo slot if the player needs enhanced defensive removal or board control that this specific evolution doesn't offer.
evolution.counters: The wiki page does not specify how the Evolution changes its counterability.

base.how_it_works: Rage is a 2 Elixir spell that provides an area-of-effect boost increasing the movement and attack speed of allied troops and buildings by 30%. It can also accelerate building summoning/firing speeds, making it effective against swarms and siege defense.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, deploy Rage when you need to punch through defensive swarms or quickly destroy a tower while minimizing opponent counterplay. Defensively, use it on slow-moving tanks (like Golems) or grouping troops to maximize their immediate impact, especially after using an initial spell.
base.counters: Strong zoning/area spells like Poison can negate the burst power of Rage by removing units before they benefit from the speed boost. High elixir denial spells, such as Tornado, force opponent unit clustering which is a prime target for Rage's increased damage and attack rate. Furthermore, strong counter-spell knowledge helps you predict when an opponent will deploy their strongest offensive pushes.
base.combos: Pairing Rage with Goblin Barrel allows the Goblins to gain significantly increased attack speed and punch through swarms while attacking the tower. When used with Electro Wizard or Musketeer against a Skeleton Army, the boosted rate of fire allows for massive wave clearing that an un-raged deploy would struggle with.
tips: Timing Rage on low-health buildings (like Cannon) can be risky; only use it if you anticipate enough accompanying high damage to finish them off before their structural HP drops too much.
Be mindful of the one-second fade duration after movement or fighting ends; this forces precise timing and placing it near key engagement points, not just far from action.
Due to its low cost, consider using Rage early in a double elixir trade when you need to force an opponent into a defensive play or prevent them from generating board control.

base.how_it_works: The Ram Rider deploys a single-target, building-targeting, melee ground troop that begins charging after traveling 2 tiles. During this charge, it deals double damage and can jump over rivers; the accompanying Rider unit snars enemies, slowing their movement speed by 70%.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, use her to initiate pressure or to capitalize on enemy mistakes, particularly when kiting troops across a bridge or utilizing buildings. Defensively, she is excellent at shutting down slow, tanky threats like P.E.K.K.A or Giant Skeleton by snaring them in place. Use her near river crossings or architectural elements (like structures/bridges) to maximize the utility of her jump ability and increased damage output.
base.counters: High-range troops are strong counters because they can attack without being engaged, allowing continuous pressure while she is out of range. Spells with stun or knockback effects (such as Lightning or Fireball) are effective last resorts to completely halt her charging attack before it hits a tower. Short-range units must close the distance directly, making them more predictable targets for strategic placement.
base.combos: Pairing Ram Rider with other building-targeting cards is highly synergistic, allowing one card to bait buildings while the other attacks unimpeded afterward. The combination also works well with Balloon or other air troops because she can attack both ground and air threats used defensively against them. Placing her behind passive structures that spawn melee units allows those units to reach the target directly for a positive Elixir trade.
tips: When kiting, wait for the enemy to cross geographical obstacles (like bridges) before deploying her to maximize jump damage and snaring efficiency.
Against high-movement troops like Elite Barbarians, position her carefully away from deep defensive structures to maintain range and allow for sustained damage/snare application.
Be aware that she prioritizes attacking non-snared units over any snared ones, making it useful against clumped, mixed-threat defenses.

base.how_it_works: The Rascals deploy a trio of units: a single-target, melee ground troop (the boy) in front, supported by two air-targeting, medium-ranged ground troops (the girls) positioned behind. The girls utilize slingshots for ranged damage while the boy acts as a tank and primary attacker.
base.how_to_use:
Offensively, position the trio to maximize splash damage potential, allowing the girls' range to chip away at targets while the boy absorbs damage. Defensively, splitting the Rascals across the arena lanes can force the opponent to dedicate multiple spells or units, especially drawing out single-target removal on the highly valuable girls.
Always prioritize protecting the Rascal Girls, as they deal higher sustained damage and are key to chipping down massive targets.
base.counters:
Spells like The Log, Arrows, and Poison effectively counter the Rascals by instantly destroying the girls, which severely diminishes the trio's offensive power. High-damage single-target units such as Valkyrie or Mega Knight can deal burst damage to eliminate the girls in one attack, allowing for a positive Elixir trade against the expensive deployment.
Lastly, any card with significant splash damage like Executioner can immediately take out all three Rascals, ensuring minimal pressure and making it an efficient defensive counter.
base.combos:
Pairing Rascals with Goblin Barrel is effective because the boy's durability allows him to absorb initial damage while forcing attention on the placed Goblins. When paired with a cheap tank like Ice Golem or Knight, these units can protect the crucial ranged girls from spells and pressure the tower simultaneously.
For defensive setups, placing them near durable structures, such as a Crown Tower or another building, ensures that even if some components die, the remaining members retain an attack angle on the objective.
tips: When defending against large tanks (e.g., P.E.K.K.A), position Rascals to allow the girls' range to continuously chip away at the tank while the boy absorbs incoming crowd damage, maximizing sustained output.

Be mindful of death damage; when anticipating a Golem or Balloon push, keep your Rascals positioned in open areas or behind other structures so they do not suffer unnecessary damage upon deployment or combat.
While powerful against single towers, remember that the high 5-Elixir cost makes them susceptible to massive global spell usage (e.g., Lightning), which can remove all three components at once.

base.how_it_works: Rocket is an area-damage spell that targets both air and ground with a small radius while inflicting knockback upon impact. It deals very high damage, making it effective for clearing clustered units or eliminating structures.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, the Rocket excels as an endgame spell to finish off weakened Crown Towers or eliminate powerful defensive structures like the X-Bow. Defensively, it is excellent at punishing high-value deployment areas by hitting support troops with a single target, such as neutralizing Mini P.E.K.K.A and its supporting units. When deployed, aim for critical areas or clustered enemy forces to maximize impact and resource efficiency.
base.counters: Electro Dragon can capitalize on the knockback effect after damage, setting up subsequent attacks. Inferno Tower is effective because while Rocket damages it, if not paired with another threat, the tower will eventually overheat and deal damage. Similarly, buildings like the Barbarian Hut are good counters because they force a positional commitment that the spell exploits.
base.combos: Pairing Rocket with funnel tactics (like using Zap or Snowball) forces the opponent to overcommit defenses, making them vulnerable to follow-up rockets on structures. Another potent combination is using it against X-Bow and Tesla: use a distraction unit first so the Inferno Tower/Tesla can activate, allowing the Rocket to destroy both components simultaneously.
tips: Do not waste high damage on mid-value single troops; instead, wait for them to spawn near structures or accompanying units to gain more value.
When targeting structures, aim precisely at the bottom corner of the Crown Tower's closest angle to minimize travel time and maximize raw output.
Due to its high cost, use Rocket primarily as a preventative measure (to deny utility or clear immediate threat) rather than as the primary damage dealer.

base.how_it_works: Royal Delivery is an area-damage spell that can only be played on your side of the arena. When cast, it deals moderate damage to enemy troops and then spawns a single Royal Recruit unit.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, use it to clear swarms or multi-ranged pushes when positioning near the Tower, capitalizing on its area damage. Defensively, drop it immediately upon seeing projectiles like Goblin Barrel or Graveyard approaching the tower to preemptively deal damage and distract remaining units. If using Tower Princess, a healthy Royal Recruit can attack the Crown Tower once after crossing the bridge, generating chip damage.
base.counters: High-HP single targets (like armored troops) may absorb the damage without effect, while dedicated control spells like Lightning or Electro Wizard can preemptively clear the spawned Royal Recruit with minimal risk. Since its damage is dealt in one hit, shielded units will only have their shields removed regardless of how many times other spells would typically strip them.
base.combos: Pairing it with Tornado is highly effective, as the spell's splash damage will obliterate all troops clumped together by Tornado simultaneously. Against Miner + Swarm, timing the drop on the Crown Tower allows the splash damage to eliminate swarms while the spawned Royal Recruit engages and distracts the Miner.
base.tips: For defense against Wizard or Witch, place Royal Delivery immediately after their support units (Skeletons) spawn; this keeps the spell's attention focused on the threat rather than its primary target. When facing ranged glass cannons across the bridge, positioning the drop right in front of them can push the enemy back slightly and force a retarget onto the spawned Recruit. Be careful using it to lure troops away from towers, as this often wastes the initial area damage.

base.how_it_works: The Royal Ghost is a ground-targeting melee troop that spawns invisibly, only turning visible when it attacks. It can still be targeted by area damage or spells while invisible. It hovers and maintains invisibility for 1.8 seconds after stopping combat.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, use him on quick pushes at the bridge to eliminate key ranged support units like Archers or Dart Goblin, capitalizing on his first strike advantage. Defensively, deploy him early against fragile ranged swarms to get a free shot and preserve hitpoints for counterplay setup. Be mindful that since he cannot kite, save him to clean up specific threats rather than relying on him for reactive tanking.
base.counters: Heavy defensive tanks like P.E.K.K.A or Three Musketeers can overwhelm his damage output if they coordinate a focused defense. High-HP, area-damage ground troops (like Skeleton Army) are effective because his slow attack speed limits his ability to clear swarms swiftly. Using cheap spells (like Zap/Snowball) at the start of an invisible push prevents him from getting critical opening hits.
base.combos: Pairing him with fast single-target units like Hog Rider or Battle Ram allows him to eliminate support troops that would otherwise threaten the main damage dealer. For defensive synergies, deploying him alongside a micro-tank (like Ice Golem) creates a highly disruptive pairing: the tank absorbs minor damage while Royal Ghost deals high burst damage to ranged threats. Use him with other area spells (e.g., Electro Dragon's attack) to ensure secondary magical hits hit him.
tips: Against enemy Goblin Drill plays, deploying him is ideal as his splash damage can efficiently clear the entire swarm even near your tower.
Due to his hover ability and invisibility reset, do not rely on him for reactionary tanking; save him for structured offensive or defensive clean-up efforts instead.
Since he ignores other Royal Ghosts, consider using him specifically against opposing support lines where stacking multiple invisible threats is valuable.

evolution.what_changes: Upon deployment, the Evolved Royal Ghost summons two Souldiers that guard his spirit and deal damage when summoned. When the Souldiers are not fighting any unit for 1.8 seconds, they disappear just like their leader.
evolution.evo_slot_value: This Evolution provides a massive boost to total damage upon attack due to the added spawn damage of Souldiers, making it powerful against single-target units and swarms. However, its high synergy with other heavy tanks or high burst setups means dedicating the slot might be less impactful if the deck struggles with controlling initial engagement.
evolution.counters: The primary threat remains countering its unit damage output; while specific counter interactions are suggested, the core strategic concern is managing the sheer damage potential when engaged by focused troops or swarms.
tips: Leverage the Souldiers' inability to despawn naturally for sustained defensive pressure and counter-push potential.
Consider pairing it with a distraction troop first so that an immediate burst of damage can be placed on the Evolved Royal Ghost, clearing off the newly summoned Souldiers.

base.how_it_works: The Royal Giant is a 6 Elixir ground troop that spawns a slow, single-target, building-targeting unit with high hitpoints and damage. Its primary combat modification is that its projectile deals area of effect (splash) damage.
base.how_to_use: Offensively, deploy the Royal Giant to create sustained pressure on towers by focusing down enemy buildings. Defensively, it can act as a subtle tank if followed up immediately with ranged melee troops while the Crown Tower prioritizes engaging the giant. A situational timing tip is using him during Double Elixir time, allowing for more aggressive pushes starting from the bridge.
base.counters: High damage swarms like Minion Horde or Skeleton Army are generally ineffective because support splash units (like Wizard) or spells (Fireball/Arrows) will wipe them out first. Similarly, high-health tanks such as P.E.K.K.A. or Mighty Miner can be deployed on top of the Royal Giant to force it back and reduce its tower damage. Other robust, fast-attacking units like Elite Barbarians are reliable due to their sheer hit points.
base.combos: Pairing the Royal Giant with a Dark Prince allows the giant to deal tower damage while the Dark Prince counter-engages enemy defenses and pushes towards the King Tower.
